held_reason: No labor range could be set for any class: no manufacturer document was found that prints a time, with a unit, for replacing one hose alone. Every maker time found is a cross-check under the review rules (a pair of hoses, a time that includes an inspection, or a time printed without a unit), and no signed guide stating a one-hose time was found. No aftermarket new price was found for any class (low parts end is null everywhere). The economy class has no example vehicle and no data at all. finding: New job, so there is no live range to judge. This file is not complete and no built total can be given: totals are parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks), and no class has a stated time for one hose that can serve as a range end. What was found. Parts: dealer list price for one genuine hose is low and consistent, $35.82 (2016 Ford Fusion), $36.10 (2014 Ram ProMaster) and $47.35 (2016 Lincoln MKX); no aftermarket new price was found, and nothing was priced for an economy car. Labor: manufacturers do print brake hose times, but every one found is a cross-check only. Ram allows 0.6 hours for one front hose and 0.5 hours for one rear hose on the 2014 ProMaster, each including an inspection of all four hoses (the inspection alone is 0.2 hours). Ford allows 1.0 Hours for both front hoses including the brake bleed on the 2015-2018 Edge and Lincoln MKX, and 1.3 Hours on the Fusion and MKZ with extra work. Ram allows 0.7 hours for both rear hose assemblies on the 4500/5500. GM prints 1.1 with no unit for one rear hose with inspection and bleed on a 2011 Express. A guide co-written by an ASE-certified mechanic gives 2-3 hours for all four hoses with bleeding. For illustration only, not a built total: the ProMaster list-price hose plus Ram's 0.6 hours comes to about $108-$132, well under every benchmark ($116-$145, $204-$266, $232-$306, $200-$450); warranty times are the low end of what shops bill and the benchmarks' labor figures alone ($105-$155 at RepairPal) are larger than that whole sum. Still needed: a one-hose time with a unit that does not include an inspection, for each class; an aftermarket new price for each class; and an economy example.
extras: A quote often adds brake fluid, new sealing washers or a banjo bolt, a scan-tool bleed on cars with ABS or stability control (one guide puts that at 0.3-0.8 hours extra), the matching hose on the other side, a full brake fluid flush, a seized hard-line fitting or a caliper if either is damaged on removal, a brake inspection fee, shop supplies and sales tax.
